tests.description: Reference: WRF 4.8 em_scm_xy single-column run (GNU real32 build, dt = 60 s, 59 layers, mp=6 ra_lw=1 ra_sw=1 sf_sfclay=1 sf_surface=1 bl_pbl=1, swrad_scat = 1, icloud = 1) dumped by the instrumented fork (module_esm_dump, SWRAD/SWPARA hooks) and replayed through the real64 (-fdefault-real-8) standalone kernels/sw_driver of the ctessum-claude/WRF fork; inputs are the dumped SWRAD arguments (single-precision values widened) of tile column 1, and every expected value is the real64 replay (the same inputs through the same Fortran in binary64, so the scheme's constants and literals are exact and the only residual is evaluation-order roundoff). The scheme is diagnostic (no time step), so no small-dt replay is involved. Column assertions are Linf_error of the whole field against the inline reference (WRF's top-down arrays reversed onto lev/lev_nodes, the top-of-atmosphere interface appended as 0 for the cumulative fields, per-cent quantities divided by 100, g/m^2 paths converted to kg/m^2); spot checks use a relative tolerance. Tolerances: measured Linf mismatch between this component and the real64 replay over all six regimes is at binary64 roundoff -- S and the cumulative depletions <= 1.2e-12 W/m^2 (1e-15 relative), U <= 4e-15 kg/m^2, W <= 1e-16 kg/m^2, the dimensionless absorptances/reflectances and layer fractions <= 4e-15, heating rates <= 1.3e-18 K/s -- so the column tolerances are set at about 1e-9 of each field's column maximum (S, D_*: abs 1e-6 W/m^2; U: 1e-8 kg/m^2; W: 1e-12 kg/m^2; rho: 1e-9 kg/m^3; m_air: 1e-7 kg/m^2; fractions: abs 1e-9; dT/dt, dtheta/dt: 1e-13 K/s), i.e. the 1e-9 relative contract for double-precision references, roughly a million times the measured error; scalar spot checks use rel 1e-9. Regime: first radiation call of the run (call 1, 19:00 UTC = 12:34 LST, cos zenith 0.629), no condensate at all (qc = qr = qs = qg = 0, qi = 0): pure clear-sky vapour absorption and scattering, the cloud tables return 0 everywhere, gsw = 542 W/m^2.

Internals are not compared at night (WRF leaves them at their zero initialisation).

Reference: WRF 4.8 em_scm_xy single-column run (GNU real32 build, dt = 60 s, 59 layers, mp=6 ra_lw=1 ra_sw=1 sf_sfclay=1 sf_surface=1 bl_pbl=1, swrad_scat = 1, icloud = 1) dumped by the instrumented fork (module_esm_dump, SWRAD/SWPARA hooks) and replayed through the real64 (-fdefault-real-8) standalone kernels/sw_driver of the ctessum-claude/WRF fork; inputs are the dumped SWRAD arguments (single-precision values widened) of tile column 1, and every expected value is the real64 replay (the same inputs through the same Fortran in binary64, so the scheme's constants and literals are exact and the only residual is evaluation-order roundoff). Regime: SYNTHETIC, Fortran-generated -- the call-120 column with a liquid stratus deck inserted (qc = 3e-4 kg/kg in the layers whose tops lie between 600 and 1500 m, about 250 g/m^2 of liquid water path on top of the cirrus), replayed through the real64 sw_driver; the SCM run itself has no liquid cloud (qc = qr = 0 throughout), so this is the only regime that drives the Stephens tables beyond their first alw interval (alw > 2, cumulative cloud albedo above 80 %) and exercises the partial-beam bookkeeping with large cloud depletion (minimum layer transmissivity well below the clear-sky values but above the 1 % renormalisation threshold tau_min, so the renormalisation factor ff is 1 everywhere and n_renorm = 0). Inputs are the modified dump synthetic_stratus_120.json; expected values are the driver output.

Reference: WRF 4.8 em_scm_xy single-column run (GNU real32 build, dt = 60 s, 59 layers, mp=6 ra_lw=1 ra_sw=1 sf_sfclay=1 sf_surface=1 bl_pbl=1, swrad_scat = 1, icloud = 1) dumped by the instrumented fork (module_esm_dump, SWRAD/SWPARA hooks) and replayed through the real64 (-fdefault-real-8) standalone kernels/sw_driver of the ctessum-claude/WRF fork; inputs are the dumped SWRAD arguments (single-precision values widened) of tile column 1, and every expected value is the real64 replay (the same inputs through the same Fortran in binary64, so the scheme's constants and literals are exact and the only residual is evaluation-order roundoff). Regime: SYNTHETIC, Fortran-generated -- the call-2400 column with the sun 2.9 degrees above the horizon (coszen = 0.05), swrad_scat = 3 (cssca = 3e-5 m^2/kg) and a surface fog of qc = 8.2e-3 kg/kg in the lowest layer (about 500 g/m^2 of liquid water, slant path 1e4 g/m^2, so the Stephens table argument sits at its clamp alw_max), replayed through the real64 sw_driver. The lowest layer's raw depletion is 95.9 % cloud + 2.3 % scattering + 1.3 % vapour = 99.5 % of the entering beam (tau_raw = 0.005 < tau_min), so SWPARA renormalises it: ff = 0.99/0.995, the applied fractions sum to 0.99, tau = 0.01 (TRANS0 = 1.), the beam reaching the surface is 1 % of the beam entering the layer and gsw = 1.9 mW/m^2. This is the only regime with n_renorm = 1; the renormalised layer is the LOWEST layer, so no depleting layer lies below it and the closed-form bookkeeping stays exact (see the S_dn description for the coupled-sweep format gap that keeps a renormalised layer with cloud or vapour below it out of the component's validity). The beam floor S_min is not reached (n_floor = 0; the bottom beam is 2.3 mW/m^2). Inputs are the modified dump synthetic_fog_2400.json; expected values are the driver output.
